study.title: Who Is the World?
study.focus: How wide is God's love, and how do the teachers read 'the world' and 'whoever believes'?
study.take: This take lets the teachers disagree in the open: Henry and Calvin read the offer as going out to all; Gill reads 'the world' as the elect among every nation. Augustine and Calvin keep the human side in view.
study.closing: Whatever you decide about the width of God's love, what does the invitation to whoever believes ask of you?

scripture.16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
scripture.17: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
scripture.18: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.

verse_questions.17: Saved: everyone, or those who believe?
verse_questions.18: Who is safe, and who is not?

summaries.MHC3.16.06: Matthew Henry says that though many perish, giving the Son was love to the whole world, since life is offered to all, like a pardon proclaimed to a rebel province.
summaries.GIL3.16.01: John Gill says world here does not mean every person. God's special love shown in giving his Son is not for all, since whoever receives the Son receives all things with him, which is not true of everyone.
summaries.CAL3.16.08: John Calvin says only-begotten is emphatic: because people find it hard to believe God loves them, God shows it by not sparing his own Son. To keep doubting after this, he says, insults Christ.
summaries.CAL3.16.09: Calvin adds that the more God values his only Son, the more precious our salvation was to him, since the Son died to ransom us. Christ is Son by nature and shares that honor with us by adoption.
summaries.CAL3.16.10: Calvin calls this high praise of faith: it frees us from everlasting destruction. The word whosoever invites everyone to life and leaves unbelievers without excuse.
summaries.CAL3.16.11: Calvin says nothing in the world deserves God's favor, yet he shows himself reconciled to the whole world by inviting all to faith. Life is promised to all who believe, but faith is not common to all.
summaries.GIL3.17.03: Gill reads the world that is saved as the elect whom God chose to save, including his chosen people among the Gentiles, which is why all the ends of the earth are called to look to him.
summaries.AUG3.17-18.1.01: Augustine pictures Christ as a physician who came to heal the sick. He came to save the world, not to judge it; whoever refuses the physician's orders destroys himself and is judged by himself.
summaries.GIL3.18.02: Gill says the believer, Jew or Gentile, is in Christ and free from condemnation. The sentence of death on all in Adam was carried out on Christ in his people's place, so whoever believes has passed from death to life and will never be condemned.
summaries.CAL3.18.02: Calvin says is not condemned means believers are safe from the fear of condemnation. The unbeliever is condemned already because there is no other remedy: life lies only in faith, so rejecting it leaves only death.

labels.jewish_source: A later Jewish writing that Gill cites; not a statement of what people believed in Jesus's day.
